title: Debugging failing health checks
idea: A health check fails when the load balancer gets no good answer from a task. ECS replaces that task, and replacements keep failing until you fix the cause.

analogy.text: A courier must reach the building, find the right door, and get a reply in time.
analogy.breaks: Couriers give up; the balancer keeps checking and ECS keeps replacing.

points: An Application Load Balancer sends `GET /` by default and expects status `200`.
Point the health check path at a simple route you own, such as `/health`.
A task turns unhealthy after `UnhealthyThresholdCount` failed checks in a row.
`healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds` tells ECS to ignore failures while a new task starts.

hero.title: Where a health check can fail

steps.caption: Every interval, the load balancer sends `GET /` to each task. Three things can break the trip.
Failure 1: the task's security group does not admit the balancer. No reply comes: `Target.Timeout`.
Fix: allow the balancer's security group to reach the container port.
Failure 2: nothing listens on that port, or the app listens only on `localhost`. The connection fails; expect `Target.FailedHealthChecks`.
Fix: listen on the port in `portMappings`, on all interfaces: `0.0.0.0`.
Failure 3: the app has no `/` route and answers 404. The reason is `Target.ResponseCodeMismatch`.
Fix: add `GET /health` that returns 200, above any auth middleware. Then set the health check path to `/health`.
The check now reaches the route, which answers 200.
The target passes its check and starts receiving requests.

code.title: Reproduce it
code.caption: Probe the API the way the balancer does, one path at a time.

walk.text: The API serves `/books`, and nothing at `/`.
`/health` answers 200 with no token and no database call.
Listen on `0.0.0.0`, all interfaces. Port `0` picks a free port for this demo.
Request `/`, the default health check path, then `/health`, and print each status.
Close the server so the script exits.

code.title: Investigate
code.caption: Work back from the balancer's verdict to the container. Angle brackets mark placeholders.

walk.text: Ask the target group why a task is unhealthy. Read `Reason` in the output.
Recent service events say when ECS stopped and replaced tasks.
List the service's stopped tasks. Do this soon; stopped tasks disappear after a while.
Read why one task stopped. A failed check says `Task failed ELB health checks`.
After adding the route, point the health check path at it.

pitfalls: Listen on `0.0.0.0`, not `localhost`; the balancer cannot reach a loopback-only server.
Choose a simple health route; a slow check, such as a database query, can time out.
Do not widen the accepted status codes to hide a 404; fix the route.

quiz.q: The balancer calls `/health` with no token. What does this print?
quiz.why: Middleware runs in order. The auth check answers 401 before the `/health` route is reached, so the balancer's check fails.

takeaway: The reason code names the failing step; fix that step, not the symptom.

starters: How long should the health check grace period be?
Why does my service keep starting and stopping tasks?
